claims.text: Spin-polarized DFT augmented with constrained magnetic moments or noncollinear spin sampling can resolve subtle magnetic energy differences at zero temperature.
The proposed method will identify a ferromagnetic configuration with lower total energy than competing non-ferromagnetic states.
The candidate material is a chemically disordered transition-metal system in a non-polarized state at 0 K.
Explicit constraints on local-moment orientations or noncollinear spin sampling can systematically sample different magnetic configurations.
The relevant structural mediator is the spatial distribution and magnitude of localized moments on transition-metal sites.
Longitudinal spin fluctuations can induce sizable magnetic moments on Co, Cr, and Ni in paramagnetic CoCrFeMnNi.
Constrained sampling forces exploration of different magnetization configurations.
Exploring different magnetization configurations makes subtle energetic advantages of parallel ferromagnetic alignment evident.
Conventional unconstrained DFT may miss delicate exchange interactions needed to stabilize a ferromagnetic ground state.
Accounting for magnetic-moment fluctuations can affect calculated energetic properties and phase stability in CoCrFeMnNi.
The ferromagnetic configuration will have lower total energy than both antiferromagnetic and paramagnetic configurations.
A lower total energy for the ferromagnetic configuration at 0 K indicates a ferromagnetic ground state.
Conventional unconstrained spin-polarized DFT does not adequately resolve small magnetic energy differences at 0 K.
The method may fail to distinguish magnetic ground states when energy differences are within the uncertainty of the DFT calculation.
Quantum fluctuations beyond static magnetic constraints may affect the ability to identify the magnetic ground state.
The precise energy margin needed to decisively establish a ferromagnetic ground state is uncertain and may be comparable to computational uncertainty.
